episodes.title: MKUltra: Why the Truth Is Worse Than You Think with Colin Ross
episodes.description: What if the most disturbing parts of MKUltra aren't the parts you've heard about? Psychiatrist Dr. Colin Ross spent decades tracking down the CIA's declassified mind control files, page by page, years before any of it was online. What he found goes far beyond LSD and a few rogue experiments. It points to the people who made it all possible, and they weren't spies. In this conversation, Dr. Roger McFillin and Tracy Thurman sit down with the author of The CIA Doctors to ask the questions most people won't: How much of Project MKUltra do we actually know? Are “Manchurian Candidates” just Hollywood fiction? And why did the medical profession stay silent while it was all published in its own journals? You'll hear about a patient who handed Dr. Ross a stack of documents that changed the direction of his career, a strange day inside a CIA reading room, and a simple test that may show how easily your own mind can be influenced. By the end, you may never look at certain moments in history, or at modern medicine, the same way again. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Dr. Roger McFillin and Tracy Thurman host Radically Genuine, challenging the systems, institutions, and ideas shaping how we think, live, heal, and understand the world around us. From medicine and mental health to technology, spirituality, institutional power, and human sovereignty, Roger and Tracy question accepted narratives, challenge what others won't, and pursue truth wherever it leads. Radically Genuine is the voice of the awakening. episodes.title: 122. Inside the Troubled Teen Treatment Industry
episodes.description: Join Elaine Walters as she recounts her journey within the controversial Straight Incorporated, a program claiming to reform teenage drug users through tough love and AA principles. However, the reality was starkly different: with no professional counseling, Straight Incorporated relied on coercive tactics, peer pressure, and mind control to recondition its participants. Elaine sheds light on the absence of adult supervision, the program's detrimental effects, and her struggle with misdiagnosis and overmedication within the psychiatric system.
